#### Structural Authority Across Registered Engineering Corners

The headline uncertainty campaign cannot legitimately reuse nominal articulated
states after changing height, body mass, or the joint-limit envelope. Those
changes alter either the model or its admissible configuration set before the
shaft and ground pathways are evaluated. A separate authority campaign therefore
regenerates all 13 phase states for headline cases 0, 8, 9, and 17 at nominal and
at six registered low/high one-at-a-time structural corners. Each JSON/NPZ pair
binds its configuration, source files, selected states, failure classes, and
array contents by digest. The atlas adapter rejects nominal-model substitution
and stops before silently omitting an infeasible selected state.

| Registered Corner | Feasible States | Maximum Closure Error (m) | Minimum Joint-Limit Margin (rad) | Minimum Collision Clearance (m) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Nominal | 52/52 | $1.03\times10^{-10}$ | 0.1035 | 0.0491 |
| Height Scale 0.90 | 51/52 | $7.80\times10^{-10}$ | $1.80\times10^{-16}$ | 0.0562 |
| Height Scale 1.10 | 52/52 | $8.94\times10^{-11}$ | 0.1806 | 0.0421 |
| Body-Mass Scale 0.85 | 52/52 | $1.03\times10^{-10}$ | 0.1035 | 0.0491 |
| Body-Mass Scale 1.15 | 52/52 | $1.03\times10^{-10}$ | 0.1035 | 0.0491 |
| Joint-Limit Scale 0.85 | 52/52 | $1.03\times10^{-10}$ | 0.0885 | 0.0491 |
| Joint-Limit Scale 1.15 | 52/52 | $1.03\times10^{-10}$ | 0.1185 | 0.0491 |

![Structural Authority Across Registered Engineering Corners](figures/fig_articulated_structural_authority.pdf){#fig-articulated-structural-authority width=100%}

Figure @fig-articulated-structural-authority keeps feasibility, joint-limit
margin, and coarse collision clearance visually distinct. Red denotes the
retained low-height failure; it does not denote a participant category or a
measured risk threshold.

The low-height corner retains one `ik_nonconvergence` result at case 0, phase
12. Its effectively zero joint-limit margin identifies a boundary-conditioned
solve in this reduced engineering model. It is neither evidence that a
corresponding human configuration is impossible nor permission to delete the
state and report 51/51 success. The unchanged geometry metrics at the two
body-mass corners are also expected: this intervention changes inertial mass
without changing segment lengths or the registered joint envelope. That
separation is a model-integrity check, not evidence that mass cannot change a
subsequent dynamic transfer result.

The campaign therefore establishes inspectable model and state authority for
the declared corners, but it does not yet establish sensitivity of either
headline estimand. Completion requires passing each feasible corner's exact
scaled model and state into both native-engine shaft and finite-ground atlases,
retaining the low-height failure in the denominator, and repeating the full
reversal, refinement, pathway-killswitch, and unchanged load--work matching
controls. A corner is falsified as propagation evidence if its configuration or
content digest fails, if a registered failure disappears, or if the atlas runs
against the nominal model instead of its bound scaled model.

The checkpointed campaign record is available as
[`articulated_structural_authority_campaign.json`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/docs/research/proximal_distal_energy_transfer/data/articulated_structural_authority_campaign.json),
with one governed JSON/NPZ pair per corner. The executable registration is
available as
[`articulated_structural_authority_campaign.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/scripts/research/proximal_distal_energy/articulated_structural_authority_campaign.py),
and the fail-closed propagation adapter is available as
[`articulated_atlas_authority.py`](https://github.com/D-sorganization/UpstreamDrift/blob/main/scripts/research/proximal_distal_energy/articulated_atlas_authority.py).
